title: Operator Gesture + Beacon Sync: Private/VPC offline handshake and acceptance criteria
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Summary: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a new Private/VPC bootstrap protocol that enables safe operator-to-control-plane handshakes in low-or-no-egress environments. The protocol combines a short-lived Operator Gesture (mutual nonce exchange) with a lightweight Beacon Sync (deferred artifact sync rendezvous) to allow operators to validate image provenance, configuration checksums, and optional KMS key exchange without requiring continuous outbound connectivity. This ticket scopes the product requirements, upgrade constraints, rollouts, and test harness needed to ship a supported offline handshake mode for Private deployments.

Background: Customers running sealed VPC or air-gapped deployments ask for an onboarding and upgrade path that does not rely on long-lived egress, but still provides strong chain-of-trust guarantees (image signing, operator identity, artifact integrity). Existing solutions rely on mirrors/mirrored registries or manual media; this protocol aims to minimize operator intervention while preserving strict network constraints.

Goals:
- Define the Operator Gesture protocol surface (messages, time windows, allowed ports, probe frequency).
- Specify Beacon Sync behavior for deferred artifact pulls and verification when periodic outbound windows are available.
- Capture upgrade acceptance criteria and rollback semantics for operator and control-plane changes during offline mode.
- Surface observability and telemetry requirements that work with restricted egress (local health endpoints, operator event logs, and encrypted telemetry bundles).

Scope:
In-scope: protocol spec, acceptance criteria, rollout plan (canary + staged), QA test matrix, monitoring contract, optional operator CLI extension.
Out-of-scope: design and implementation of physical media workflows, full airgap appliance (separate ticket), or provider-specific mirror tooling.
acceptance_criteria: Operator Gesture exchange is defined: nonce challenge, operator cert signing validation, and 3 retry windows (1 min, 5 min, 30 min) documented and implemented in operator code path.

Beacon Sync contract establishes a deferred pull handshake: control plane publishes artifact manifest with signed checkpoint; operator can fetch only during pre-authorized egress window and must validate signing before applying artifacts.
All network requirements limited to a single allowed outbound port range (e.g., 443 and a configured mirror port), documented with IP/dns allowlist patterns for customer firewall policy.

Upgrade acceptance: rolling upgrade plan for operator when in offline mode with ability to abort and rollback within N minutes (configurable, default 30) without requiring outbound connectivity to Redwood control plane.

Telemetry requirements for offline mode: operator emits local event bundles, persisted to disk, and a scheduled encrypted bundle uploader that triggers only during authorized egress windows; schema and retention policy documented.
Security gates: KMS rotation and key exchange flow works with pre-shared envelope keys; handshake fails closed and surfaces explicit operator action required in UI/CLI when cryptographic checks fail.

Automated test harness: end-to-end CI job simulates sealed VPC with blocked egress, verifies handshake success/failure modes and rollback semantics across at least three kernel versions and two image signing keys.
Customer-facing documentation: onboarding checklist, minimal firewall rules doc, operator CLI commands, and troubleshooting matrix published in product docs.
PM + Security sign-off obtained prior to release; a documented threat model and short privacy impact assessment are attached to the release PR.
decisions: Adopt two-phase model: short-lived Operator Gesture for identity validation, followed by Beacon Sync for artifact transfer when egress window is available.
Default retry windows for the gesture will be conservative (1m, 5m, 30m) but configurable by site operator in advanced settings.
Telemetry will be buffered locally and uploaded only during pre-scheduled egress windows; we will use envelope encryption to protect contents in transit.
Operator upgrade rollback will be implemented as a coordinated two-step: local node rollback + control-plane checkpoint revert; both steps must be test-covered in offline simulation.
Prefer manifest-level signatures (not per-file) to reduce bandwidth and verification surface for deferred syncs.
open_questions: Do we require customers to provide a dedicated bastion IP for the initial gesture, or can nonce exchange work via signed static manifests delivered through physical media?
What is the minimal set of ports/custom DNS names that SOC teams will accept as 'allowlistable' across large regulated customers?
How should operator-initiated key rotation be surfaced in the Console vs CLI for Private deployments with no console connectivity?
Should we support a passive-mode Beacon that only validates and never auto-applies artifacts unless explicitly confirmed by an operator?
